w: At 10.50 am Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of the murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni in the hall beneath the mandir podium. Thereafter Swamishri performed pujan and bathed the murtis with panchamrut and water mixed with saffron. Then in his blessings to the devotees Swamishri said, "We first consecrated the murti of Nilkanth Varni in Bharuch and then abroad in Toronto, Chicago and London. Whosoever comes for darshan of this murti an performs abhishek (oblation) will have his wishes fulfilled. His problems too will be solved. But you need to have faith. If you have faith then your wishes will be realized. So you should offer devotion with your mind, body and wealth. Shabri was a tribal woman, but she remembered Ram with inner faith and thus Ram came..."

ds.t: Shake off the burden of thoughts
w: Years ago, a spiritual seeker had taken his own life and passed away. His son, though very bright in his studies, could not erase from his mind the effect of the scenes he had seen in childhood. This teenager, studying in the twelfth standard, kept telling his mother, "Every year I have got over 80% marks. But if I get low marks in the twelfth standard, I too will take my life like my father."

For the mother, who had lost the shelter of her husband, these words of her son were like a thunderbolt. What else could she do for her only beloved son? So today she had sent him to Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Blessing him, Swamishri said, "Work hard and do bhajan and devotion, so that there is no burden on your mind. Every year you get the best marks, so why do you think weak thoughts now? You should think only that you are certainly going to pass with good marks. If you lose heart from now, you will not be able to write or read. So do not think weak thoughts at all. Work hard and move ahead. Do not keep the burden on your mind that you will get low marks. Do bhajan of Shriji Maharaj and pray. We will also pray for you. You are certainly going to get good marks. Even if by chance you do not get good marks, do not be afraid. Even people with no education at all have moved ahead. People like Dhirubhai Ambani studied only a little, but moved ahead by their own intelligence and skill. So do not think anything else about marks. Work hard with the thought that you will certainly get good marks."

Swamishri filled the teenager's heart with hope. Then Swamishri went on to say to him, "Even if obstacles come, do not give up firmness in your goal. How many obstacles came to Shastriji Maharaj? But he was resolved in his mind to spread the knowledge of Akshar Purushottam, so he did not look at any obstacle. The path of the great person is before us. So we should act in that way. If you keep faith and work hard, you will move ahead."

The preliminary rituals of mandir patosav and pratishtha of the new guru parampara murtis were performed by senior sadhus. Swamishri performed the patotsav and pratishtha arti after completing his morning puja. More than 25,000 devotees had come for the morning puja darshan. Senior sadhus garlanded Swamishri and honoured him on his 70th diksha anniversary. An annakut was offered in all three shrines of Thakorji in the main mandir.

In the Sunday evening satsang assembly Viveksagar Swami and Kothari Swami discoursed to the mammoth gathering. The kothari of Surat mandir, Uttamprakash Swami, announced Swamishri’s wish that with the prevailing financial recession, which has direly affected the diamond industry, there would be no Jholi Utsav, but a simple satsang assembly would be held. Dhun was sung, as prayers, to resolve the financial crisis. The kishores and yuvaks performed a cultural dance. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly, “You all came this morning for the patotsav, and have come again this evening for satsang. This reflects upon your heartfelt devotion and faith in God. Through these two things one attains inner peace. Presently, there is an economic recession and it is understandable that you are all very worried. But despite this, the important thing is to have firm refuge in God. By having faith and trust in God you will be able to hurdle over the problems. God is the all-doer. When businesses are prospering one feels God is very gracious, but when such a crisis comes one feels that God is not doing anything to improve things. But this is not so. God does good for all. He comes on earth to liberate all…”

Jitendra, the grandson of Ambalalbhai (Bakripol), had come from New Jersey. He was sitting among all the devotees in Yogi Mandapam. Since childhood he had sung many kirtans in Pramukh Swami Maharaj's puja, and Swamishri still has the memory engraved that Jitu sings kirtans. In between, because of business and so on, he could not come to satsang regularly, but for the last year he has become active again.
As soon as he saw him sitting far away, Swamishri said, "Jitu! How are you? You still sing kirtans, don't you?"
"Yes, I sing."
Swamishri said, "Then come upstairs and sing in the puja."
The sadhus said, "But today Shivamani's programme has been arranged."
Swamishri said, "Then no problem. You have my blessings."

Today, when Mahant Swami Maharaj had completed his regular walk and finally sat in a chair to rest, the sadhus brought a beautiful rabbit from among those kept here on the premises. Swamishri seated it on his right thigh and began to play with it. Swamishri was lovingly stroking the whole body of that fortunate rabbit. He was also caressing its ears. The rabbit too calmly enjoyed the touch, as if it had been waiting for this touch for countless births.
The sadhus said, "Swami! Its next birth in satsang is certain, isn't it?"
Swamishri, pleased, said "Yes". Then the sadhus put forward another point: "But Swami! It is in your hands, it can be liberated directly too. Isn't that right?"
Swamishri said "Yes".
It was time to go. So the rabbit was set free. Then, happily refreshing old memories, Swamishri said, "In Bangkok I stroked a tiger!"
The sadhus said, "Then that too is liberated! Isn't that right!"
Swamishri said yes. Then he said, "The elephant on which Shastriji Maharaj rode in procession passed away to Akshardham within seven days."
The sadhus immediately said, "Then this rabbit...!"
Then Swamishri said, "No, no, this one will stay. It will go in whatever way it is meant to go."
